clue.text: Flier, tough to manage, some recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pilot who is hard to handle, and some people are being recalled from duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals letters hidden across 'tough to manage' (HTOM), and 'recalled' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-flying insect with wings is quite literally a flier.

clue.text: Gathered to bring in silver (new) that's attractive

indicators.note: to bring in says the gathered word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: met means gathered together, assembled
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: People assembled to bring in new silverware, which is very appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's attractive' reads as a comment on the surface, but it is the definition: a thing that attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: An object that draws iron or a person who draws others is something that attracts.

clue.text: Determined action — sue for reconstruction

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds something, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A resolute legal step: take someone to court to pay for rebuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent and unwilling to let go is a synonym for determined.

clue.text: More sensual side introduced by son? That's right

indicators.note: the side is introduced by the son, so his letter comes first in the charade

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
that's, i.e. 'that is', is abbreviated IE

explanation.surface: A sports team being shown off by a young man is somehow sexier — is that correct?
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy is informal for erotic or passionate, so its comparative means more sensual.

clue.text: Sweet stuff, torte, parcelled oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of the words torte and parcelled

explanation.surface: A cake was wrapped up in a strange fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark syrup from sugar refining is a sweet, sticky substance, or golden syrup used in a tart.

clue.text: How chintz is arranged

parts.note: chintz is a floral fabric, but here the word itself: its letters C, H, I, N, T, Z run in order from A to Z

explanation.surface: A question of how a patterned furnishing fabric is laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to fabric design; it is about the spelling, whose letters each follow the previous one in the standard order.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters of the word stand in the order of the ABC, so the word is sorted that way.

clue.text: Old people's reserve, popular when brought up

parts.note: ice means reserve, a cold aloof manner

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Elderly folk's reticence is fashionable when raised in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses IN to NI below ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca's tribe of ancient Britons was a people of the distant past.

clue.text: She's optimistic about newly-trained mare

indicators.note: about says the optimistic word goes round the other letters

parts.note: rosy means hopeful, optimistic

indicators.note: a newly-trained horse is re-schooled, so the letters of mare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is hopeful about her freshly schooled horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-trained' gives EMAR from the mare, and 'about' wraps the optimistic word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, and She stands for any female person.

clue.text: Neat feature in place to retire. Guy's niche?

definitions.text: Neat feature in place to retire
definitions.meaning: a tidy fold of sheets at the end of a made bed, the place one retires to at night
Guy's is a famous London infirmary, and a niche is a nook, so this is a playful picture of a nook in that building

explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a well-known London teaching hospital; the second reading takes the answer literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The tightly tucked sheet fold used by nurses is a tidy bed-making technique.

clue.text: Perm finally in hairdresser's place for swimmer

indicators.note: in says the last letter goes inside the hairdresser's place

parts.note: a salon is a hairdresser's premises

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word Perm

explanation.surface: A perm at last at the hairdresser's for a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish that swims upriver to spawn is a swimmer, a crossword term for any fish.

clue.text: Party in a long foreign craft

indicators.note: in says the party is placed inside the rearranged letters
foreign suggests strange or alien, so the letters of a long are made unfamiliar by rearranging

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A celebration held aboard a lengthy boat from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges A LONG into GONLA, and 'in' places DO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boat propelled by a standing oarsman is a kind of craft, meaning a vessel.

clue.text: First pair of emigrants joining crowd in Victoria, say

indicators.note: first pair of takes the opening two letters of the word emigrants

parts.note: to crowd or throng is to press

explanation.surface: Emigrants arriving at the Victoria terminus join the throng there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the London station or the Australian state; it is Queen Victoria, Empress of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria held the title Empress of India, so she is an example of a female imperial ruler.

clue.text: Nice speech mama's prepared — it may be needed 21?

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a way out one might want after a regretted night

indicators.note: a prepared speech is worked up in advance, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother has drafted a pleasant address — perhaps you will want to flee from it the following day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the answer of 21 across: on that regretful day one may want a way out of the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological defence or literal way out is wanted when one regrets the previous night's behaviour.

clue.text: Persist in using withdrawn basic measure in motorway feature?

indicators.note: the second in says the reversed unit sits inside the motorway feature

parts.note: traffic cones are a familiar sight at motorway roadworks

indicators.note: withdrawn suggests drawn back, so the word for a basic measure is read backwards

parts.note: a unit is a basic measure of quantity

explanation.surface: Keep on with a measurement that has been scrapped, found at roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' reverses the basic measure to TINU; the second 'in' places it inside the traffic cone, a British motorway roadworks fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on employing something, such as a drug or method, is to keep on with it.

clue.text: Impatiently desiring drink getting euro at outset for pounds

indicators.note: getting introduces the replacement letter that the drink receives
at outset for says the swap happens at the start, the new letter taking the old one's place

parts.note: lager is a drink, a light beer
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A thirsty person wanting a pint finds euros at the start replacing pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'at outset for' together swap the first letter of LAGER, L, for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen and longing for something is a direct synonym of impatiently desiring.

clue.text: Occasional visitor glassed?

parts.note: a pub ale stocked for a short time only is an occasional visitor to the bar, and it is served in a glass

explanation.surface: Was an infrequent caller attacked with a broken bottle?
explanation.walkthrough: 'glassed' suggests a pub assault; it means poured into a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's temporary ale, offered for a limited period, is a visitor in the drinking sense.

clue.text: Former pupil's story involving constant showjumping feature

parts.note: an OB is an old boy, a former pupil, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: involving means including, so the story takes the constant inside it

parts.note: a tale is a story
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: An old boy's tale about an ever-present show-jumping hurdle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence or wall that a horse must clear is a hurdle in a showjumping course.

clue.text: Graduate's with the Italian guy

parts.note: a BA is a graduate (Bachelor of Arts), plus the S of the possessive
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A graduate's companion is the Italian man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's name, and guy is a crossword's way of signalling a male first name.

clue.text: School mentor's No 1 reject having been accepted for United?

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the school takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school

indicators.note: No 1 points to the first letter of the word mentor's

parts.note: to bin something is to reject it

explanation.surface: A mentor's top pupil was refused but then admitted to Manchester United?
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club; it is the plain adjective. A coed is a school for both sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined together or merged means the same as united.

clue.text: Hostile to North, this person's to scheme underhandedly

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
this person is the setter, I, so this person's gives I've, I have

explanation.surface: An enemy of the North says he has plotted in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire or plot secretly is to scheme in an underhand way.

clue.text: Household of soldiers, mature

parts.note: men are soldiers, the ranks
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A family home full of grown-up troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word for a domestic establishment or group of people living together.

clue.text: Initially beau gagging for it — that's fine maybe

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word beau

parts.note: British slang for desperate for sex, which is randy, lustful

explanation.surface: A boyfriend eager for sex — and that is perfectly all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gagging for it' is British slang for very keen on sex. 'fine' is not the adjective: fine is a grade of cognac.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine is a type of French spirit, so a fine is an example of this spirit.

clue.text: Ordered ninth? AM of regret!

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ninth drink ordered, followed by a morning of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: drinks ordered late at night lead to a hungover dawn of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the following day's dawn, when one regrets the excesses of the night before.

clue.text: Contest level over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: even means level, flat

explanation.surface: A competition that is drawn after full time.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition or race at a sports meeting is a contest.

clue.text: Letter in Greek about Queen backing city

indicators.note: about says the Greek letter goes round the other piece

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the queen's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A Greek letter about a queen supporting a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the queen's name to ENNA, and 'about' wraps the Greek letter round it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian city, formerly Madras, is the capital of Tamil Nadu.

clue.text: Bitterness linked to long time in ship

indicators.note: linked to joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour
an eon is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: Resentment connected with a lengthy spell aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing warship of the sixteenth century is an example of a ship.

clue.text: Former journalist admitting offence taken after threats

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the offence goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former
ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist
a tort is a civil wrong, an offence in law

explanation.surface: An ex-reporter confesses to a crime committed under duress.
explanation.definitionFit: Money obtained by blackmail or intimidation is forced out of someone, gained through coercion.

clue.text: Carrier in Tangier evacuated? Indeed

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word Tangier remain

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word meaning yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A transport vehicle in a Moroccan port emptied of people? Yes indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board for holding cups and plates is a carrier of food and drinks.
